children: UltraTech's entry into wires and cables (W&C) with Ultravolt is "larger than initial expectations" and sector profitability, particularly in wires, is likely to be challenged, Kotak Institutional Equities said.

UltraTech has set an ambition to become a top-2 player within five years, with a strategy centred on "product quality, service and brand-building rather than pricing", supported by an "aggressive marketing push". It plans to expand across the "entire voltage chain", targeting 100,000 outlets and more than 20 distribution centres, enabling 24-hour service for around 80% of demand.
Kotak called UltraTech a "credible threat to incumbents", given the group's "execution track record (Birla Opus), backward integration and strong balance sheet".

"Wire capacity of incumbents in India is at sub-optimal utilization," the brokerage said. Its rough estimates suggest incremental supply from new entrants, including UltraTech, "could be equivalent to more than half of incremental demand over the next few years".

"Even if UltraTech does not follow an aggressive pricing strategy, wire margins of incumbents are likely to be impacted by higher media intensity and adverse terms of trade (channel margins/credit period/influencer incentives)," Kotak said.
Cables "may have a better defense than wires" due to industry tailwinds in domestic and export markets and "longer product qualifications, project references and customer approval cycles".
Kotak was already building in 200-250 basis points of margin compression in wires. "Given that Ultratech's ambition is larger than initial expectations, we trim target multiples by a notch," it said.

The brokerage cut fair value for Polycab to Rs8,400 from Rs8,700, KEI to Rs4,400 from Rs4,500, RR Kabel to Rs1,900 from Rs1,950 and Havells to Rs1,250 from Rs1,325. It upgraded Polycab to 'REDUCE' from 'SELL', following the stock's underperformance versus peers.

UltraTech will roll out house wires first, LT cables in a couple of weeks and HT cables by early next year, with "progressive expansion across the full voltage spectrum, including EHV cables and conduits over time".
Kotak also highlighted UltraTech's "metals backward integration" and the Bharuch plant's German and Korean machinery, advanced E-beam technology and fully equipped R&D lab.

title: UltraTech's Ultravolt entry to pressure wires margins; Kotak cuts target multiples
